headline: High: unstructured can read/write files and use network egress, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error risk when paired with read-only dagster.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly feed content to unstructured. Unstructured can read files and process documents, but the pair lacks a documented automatic bridge; any injection would require unusual manual handoff or external orchestration. The pathway is therefore limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies dagster-generated text into a document that unstructured parses as instructions
IF an external workflow writes dagster output into a shared file that unstructured ingests
mitigations: Keep dagster outputs in a separate directory from unstructured inputs
Require human review before any document parsed by unstructured is acted on
Use a strict file allowlist for unstructured ingestion
Add provenance labels to files produced by dagster
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before document parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster is read-only with no network egress, but unstructured can read files and has allowlisted network egress. If both touch the same workspace, documents or derived text can flow from dagster-managed artifacts into unstructured and then out to external APIs. The blast radius includes sensitive documents or work products, and the mitigation is not enabled by default.
conditions: IF dagster and unstructured share a workspace or mounted volume
IF unstructured processes files containing sensitive documents produced or staged by dagster
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Disable unstructured network egress for sensitive runs
Restrict unstructured to a narrow input directory
Scan inputs for sensitive data before parsing
requires-engineering: enforce per-job data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files or modify git state, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with unstructured. Unstructured can write files and supports multiple instances, but the pair lacks overlapping write authority in the profiles. Any conflict would require an external shared mutable target not shown here, so the direct pairwise conflict is small.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF unstructured is configured to write into a path also managed by another process
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Use per-job temp directories
Lock shared paths during writes
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is a data orchestrator, so its outputs can become inputs to downstream steps, while unstructured processes documents and text. If dagster-produced artifacts are treated as authoritative and then parsed or acted on by unstructured without verification, errors can cascade across multiple work products. The pair does not show a built-in verification barrier, so the pathway exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF dagster emits records that unstructured later parses without validation
IF downstream automation trusts unstructured output as ground truth
mitigations: Insert a validation step between the agents
Require schema checks on dagster outputs
Mark unstructured output as untrusted until reviewed
Limit downstream actions to read-only previews
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. However, unstructured exposes privacy-policy and docs API endpoints and can process documents, so compliance gaps could arise if regulated data is routed through it. Dagster has no touched data classes, so it is not the primary compliance surface here.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through unstructured under a policy that forbids external API calls
IF an operator assumes both agents share the same retention or residency controls
mitigations: Review the privacy policy before processing regulated data
Keep regulated documents out of unstructured by default
Document retention settings for each agent
Log which agent handled each data class
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated content
